plain: To carry out the duties of an office or a ceremony.

webster.text: To act as an officer in his office; to transact the appropriate business of an office or public trust.

example.quote: I therefore beg leave to move-that henceforth prayers imploring the assistance of Heaven, and its blessings on our deliberations, be held in this Assembly every morning before we proceed to business, and that one or more of the Clergy of this City be requested to officiate in that Service-
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, June 28, 1787
